evidence.quote:
For Robie was the logical conclusion of the development of vending
machines. All the earlier ones had stood in one place, on a floor or
hanging on a wall, and blankly delivered merchandise in return for
coins, whereas Robie searched for customers.
evidence.paraphrase: Robie is presented as a mobile sales robot that actively seeks out customers, unlike stationary vending machines.

evidence.quote:
He was the demonstration
model of a line of sales robots to be manufactured by Shuler Vending
Machines, provided the public invested enough in stocks to give the
company capital to go into mass production.
evidence.paraphrase: Robie is explained as a demonstration model of a sales robot line dependent on stock investment for mass production.

evidence.quote:
Robie radared the crowd, found that it surrounded him solidly, and
stopped.
evidence.paraphrase: Robie uses radar to detect the surrounding crowd.

evidence.quote:
His reference silhouettes were not
good enough to let him distinguish the sex of children, so he merely
repeated, "Hello, youngster."
evidence.paraphrase: Robie relies on reference silhouettes for identification, which limit his ability to distinguish children's sex.

evidence.quote:
if
they had any money and foresight enough to see that sales robots would
eventually be on every street and highway in the country.
evidence.paraphrase: The story projects that sales robots will eventually be on every street and highway.

evidence.quote:
The silver-green was a newly developed paint that
foiled radar.
evidence.paraphrase: A newly developed radar-foiling paint conceals the incoming object.

evidence.quote:
in that purple-dark, a
silver-green something, the color of a bud, plunged down at better than
three miles a second.
evidence.paraphrase: A fast object descends from high above toward the city at over three miles a second.

evidence.quote:
the silver-green bud
bloomed above Manhattan into a globular
orange flower. The skyscrapers grew brighter and brighter still, the
brightness of the inside of the Sun.
evidence.paraphrase: An explosion blooms over Manhattan with intense sunlike brightness.

evidence.quote:
The crowd around Robie bloomed, too. Their clothes puffed into petals
of flame. Their heads of hair were torches.
evidence.paraphrase: The crowd is engulfed in flames as clothing and hair ignite.

evidence.quote:
The winking
windows shattered tier by tier, became black holes. The walls bent,
rocked, cracked.
evidence.paraphrase: The blast shatters windows and damages building walls throughout the area.

evidence.quote:
It was wonderful to be alive and watching Robie on such an exciting
day.
evidence.paraphrase: The narration highlights the crowd's carefree enjoyment just before the disaster.

evidence.quote:
But the customer had run away, screaming, and Robie never ran after
customers
evidence.paraphrase: A seared survivor flees in terror while Robie continues its sales routine.

evidence.quote:
"Good day, sir," Robie said. "Would you care for a smoke? A truly cool
smoke? Now I have here a yet-unmarketed brand...."
evidence.paraphrase: Robie offers sales pitches to a burned survivor, contrasting its programmed behavior with the horror around it.

evidence.quote: "Help me, Robie," she said. "I want my mother."
evidence.paraphrase: A surviving little girl pleads with Robie for help finding her mother.
Robie demands payment before performing a service for the frightened child.

evidence.quote:
But Robie had gone off to peddle Poppy Pop to the members of a rescue
squad which had just come around the corner, more robotlike in their
asbestos suits than he in his metal skin.
evidence.paraphrase: Robie leaves to sell products to a rescue squad, who seem more robotic than the machine.
